plain_explanation: A way of counting part-time students or staff as fractions of a full-time one, so that schools with many part-timers can be compared with schools that have few. For staff, IPEDS adds one-third of the part-time staff to the full-time staff. For students, IPEDS has two calculations: one from fall headcounts and one from the 12-month instructional activity (credit or clock hours).
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Full-time equivalent (FTE) of staff; Full-time equivalent (FTE) of students
evidence: Owner question (5f): "What does FTE mean?"; shown in measure names (core expenses per FTE student, student-to-faculty ratio)

plain_explanation: The group of students a rate is calculated on, after IPEDS's allowed exclusions are taken out: students who died, became permanently disabled, left for military service, a foreign aid service, or an official church mission. Graduation and retention rates divide by the adjusted cohort, not by everyone who started.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Adjusted cohort; Cohort
evidence: Owner question (5f): "What is an adjusted cohort?"; shown in rate definitions and Outcome Measures names

plain_explanation: Retention, as IPEDS reports it, is the share of first-time students who come back to the same school the next fall. Persistence usually means staying enrolled anywhere, including at another school; IPEDS does not publish a persistence rate. Outcome Measures come closest, by reporting students who later enrolled at another institution.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Retention rate; Outcome Measures (OM). Persistence is not in the glossary: general explanation
evidence: Owner question (5f): "What's the difference between retention and persistence?"; IR concept that changes how a number is read

words: sticker price; published tuition; total price; net price
plain_explanation: The published (sticker) price is what a school lists: tuition and fees, food and housing, books and other expenses for a full-time, first-time student. Net price is what such students who received grant or scholarship aid paid on average, after that aid. Net price is usually far lower, and it differs by family income.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Net price; Cost of attendance (COA)
evidence: Owner questions (5f, 6): "What's the difference between sticker price and net price?", "Total price or net price, which should I use to compare affordability?"
app_convention: terms.csv 'net price': the default is students awarded grant or scholarship aid

concept: Why net price is a year behind
plain_explanation: IPEDS collects net price for the year before the release's own year, because it depends on the aid students actually received, which is only known after that year ends. So the 2024-25 release reports net price for 2023-24.
source: terms.csv statement on net price; year_meaning.csv (COST2_NETPRICE)
evidence: Owner question (5f): "Why is net price a year behind?"; a statement the app already shows
app_convention: terms.csv statement: Net price is reported one year behind the rest of the release

words: graduation rate; transfer students; 150%; normal time
plain_explanation: The IPEDS graduation rate follows only students who started at the school as first-time, full-time students, and counts those who finished there within 150% of normal time (six years for a bachelor's degree). Students who transfer in are not in the cohort, and students who transfer out and finish elsewhere do not count as graduates. Outcome Measures add part-time and transfer-in students and report awards at four, six and eight years.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Graduation rate; Normal time to completion; Transfer-out student; Outcome Measures (OM)
evidence: Owner question (5f): "Why doesn't the IPEDS graduation rate count transfer students?"; owner question (6) on graduation rate versus Outcome Measures

plain_explanation: Each IPEDS release is first published as provisional data, after NCES's checks. A year later it is published again as final data, which includes the corrections schools made in the meantime. The figures can change a little between the two. In this app, 2024-25 is provisional and the other nine releases are final.
source: IPEDS overview 2019 (pages 10-11, data quality and release); _releases table in this app
evidence: Owner question (5f): "What does 'provisional' mean in IPEDS?"; the app shows a provisional warning on every 2024-25 answer
app_convention: The warning on answers from the 2024-25 release

plain_explanation: A school that has an agreement with the U.S. Department of Education to take part in federal student aid programs (Pell Grants and federal loans). Taking part in IPEDS is required for these schools and voluntary for others, so IPEDS is most complete for Title IV schools.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Title IV institution; IPEDS overview 2019 (page 1)
evidence: Owner question (5f): "What is a Title IV institution?"; part of the app's national universe statement
app_convention: terms.csv 'national universe': Title IV participating schools

plain_explanation: The group of schools a school's own IPEDS Data Feedback Report compares it with. The school can choose it, or NCES builds it from similar schools. In this app, "its peers" means that group, as of the latest year.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Comparison group; CUSTOMCGIDS table in this app
evidence: Owner question (5f): "What is the IPEDS comparison group?"; the app's "its peers" reading
app_convention: terms.csv 'peers': the school's own IPEDS comparison group

concept: The national universe in this app
words: national universe; all U.S. schools; nationally
plain_explanation: When no group is named, this app counts schools in the 50 states and DC that take part in Title IV federal aid, leaving out administrative offices (system offices that enroll no students). IPEDS itself also holds schools in U.S. territories and some that do not take part in Title IV.
source: IPEDS overview 2019 (page 8: the IPEDS universe); terms.csv 'national universe'
evidence: Words the app shows in Interpreted as on every national figure

words: parent; child; reports with; branch campus
plain_explanation: Some schools report part of their IPEDS data together with another campus of the same institution. The parent reports the combined figures, and the child's own figures are blank or zero for that part. This app says so when a school's figures come from a related campus.
source: IPEDS overview 2019 (page 2: branch campuses); FLAGS table (parent/child indicators); terms.csv 'related campus'
evidence: Words the app shows in notes (related campus)

plain_explanation: When a school does not report, or leaves some items blank, NCES estimates the missing figures so national totals are complete. Imputed figures are estimates, not the school's own report. They are flagged in the IPEDS data.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Imputation; IPEDS overview 2019 (page 11)
evidence: How IPEDS works (work order list); affects school-level figures

plain_explanation: Students who are at college for the first time, at any school, and are enrolled full time. Many IPEDS rates (graduation, retention, net price) are only about this group, not about all students.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: First-time student (undergraduate); Full-time student
evidence: Words the app shows in measure names and definitions

plain_explanation: Fall enrollment counts students enrolled on the school's fall census date. 12-month enrollment counts every student enrolled at any time in a full year (July to June), each counted once. The 12-month count is larger, especially at community colleges with many short-term or part-time students.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Fall Enrollment (EF); 12-month enrollment (E12)
evidence: Owner question (6): "Fall enrollment or 12-month enrollment?"
app_convention: terms.csv 'enrollment': fall total headcount is the default

plain_explanation: Instructional staff are people whose main job is teaching (or teaching with research or public service). Faculty status is a separate label the school gives some staff, often with rank and tenure. The two counts overlap but are not the same.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Instructional Staff; Faculty
evidence: Owner question (6): "Instructional staff or faculty with faculty status?"

concept: Pell grants as an income measure
plain_explanation: IPEDS does not collect family income for all students. The share of undergraduates with a Pell Grant, which goes to students with financial need, is the usual stand-in for the share of lower-income students. It is a proxy, not a count of low-income students.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Pell Grant program; terms.csv 'low-income' statement
evidence: Owner question (6): "How can I tell how well a college serves low-income students?"; IR concept; the app's own statement
app_convention: terms.csv 'low-income': IPEDS does not measure income; the Pell share is a common proxy

plain_explanation: The graduation rate follows first-time, full-time students only, at 150% of normal time. Outcome Measures follow four groups (first-time and not first-time, full time and part time) and report awards at four, six and eight years, and where students without an award are enrolled. Outcome Measures describe more of a community college's students.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Graduation rate; Outcome Measures (OM)
evidence: Owner question (6): "Should I use the graduation rate or the Outcome Measures award rate?"

plain_explanation: A school that awards associate's or higher degrees. Many IPEDS statistics, such as the NCES tables, cover degree-granting schools only.
source: IPEDS overview 2019; HD.DEGGRANT in this app
evidence: Words the app shows in group names and statements

plain_explanation: A classification of U.S. colleges by mission and the degrees they award, developed by the Carnegie Foundation and now kept by the American Council on Education. IPEDS carries it as a school characteristic. This app uses the 2021 basic classification as of 2024-25 for every year.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26: Carnegie Classification; DECISIONS.md (Carnegie groups in a trend)
evidence: Words the app shows in group names
app_convention: Carnegie groups use the stated classification for every year

words: GASB; FASB; finance forms; net position; net assets
plain_explanation: Public schools report finance using government accounting standards (GASB), private nonprofit schools using nonprofit standards (FASB), and for-profit schools on their own form. The forms name and group items differently, so finance figures are only roughly comparable across the three.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26 (GASB and FASB entries); terms.csv 'different reporting forms'
evidence: A statement the app shows on finance answers; owner question (6) on financial health
app_convention: terms.csv statement: finance figures are reported on three forms

words: release year; academic year; fiscal year; data year
plain_explanation: Each IPEDS release mixes periods. The 2024-25 release has fall 2024 enrollment, but completions and finance for the year before, and net price for the year before that. This app shows each figure's own period beside it.
source: year_meaning.csv in this app
evidence: Words the app shows in every answer's period

plain_explanation: A blank in IPEDS can mean the school did not report the item, or that the item does not apply to it (a school with no graduate students reports no graduate enrollment). This app never counts either as zero, and says which one it is where IPEDS records it.
source: special_codes.csv and _missing_reasons in this app
evidence: Words the app shows in the data status

plain_explanation: The admission rate is admitted applicants divided by all applicants, from schools that do not admit everyone. A low rate is often read as selectivity, but it also depends on how many students apply. IPEDS reports test scores and yield beside it.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26 (Applicant; Admissions); terms.csv 'admission rate'
evidence: Owner question (6): "What's a good measure of how selective a school is?"

plain_explanation: Students who are admitted and intend to enroll in the spring, but do not show up in the fall. IPEDS does not measure it directly; the closest figures are the admission yield (admitted students who enrolled) and fall enrollment of first-time students.
source: General explanation (not in the glossary or the overview)
evidence: Owner question (5f): "What is 'summer melt'?"

plain_explanation: IPEDS has two kinds of private school: nonprofit and for-profit. In this app, "private" alone is read as private nonprofit; say "for-profit" to include those schools.
source: IPEDS glossary 2025-26 (Private not-for-profit institution; Private for-profit institution); school_groups.csv
evidence: An app convention the work order names (Part 5f example)
app_convention: school_groups.csv 'Private not-for-profit': words "private nonprofit; private; private colleges"

plain_explanation: A U.S. Department of Education website that combines IPEDS data with federal student aid and tax records, for earnings, debt and repayment. Those earnings and debt figures are not in IPEDS.
source: General explanation; outside_ipeds.csv (earnings, debt)
evidence: Question log: "What is college scorecard"
app_convention: outside_ipeds.csv rows on earnings and debt
